description: Punctuation and formatting tics that cluster in AI output. The em dash is the most documented single tell in AI detection literature.

punctuation.pattern: The long dash used as a parenthesis or dramatic pause, multiple times per paragraph
punctuation.tell: Flat for a decade, then surged in LLM-era text. Most detectors weight it heavily. Overuse is the tell - one or two per document is normal human usage.
punctuation.fix: Replace with commas, parentheses, or split sentences. If you keep any, keep one per page at most.

punctuation.pattern: Colon used to reveal a payoff at least once per paragraph
punctuation.tell: AI uses the colon setup-reveal construction as a default dramatic device.
punctuation.fix: Write the payoff as the sentence.

punctuation.pattern: Semicolons joining clauses that should be separate sentences
punctuation.tell: AI overuses semicolons to vary rhythm. Heavy semicolon use reads academic-AI.
punctuation.fix: Split into two sentences. Keep a semicolon only where the two halves genuinely interlock.

punctuation.pattern: Trailing ... at the end of thoughts, or multiple in one paragraph
punctuation.tell: AI fakes contemplative hesitation with ellipses.
punctuation.fix: Use a period. If quoting someone trailing off, keep one.

punctuation.pattern: Two or more exclamation marks, or exclamations on neutral statements
punctuation.tell: AI adds exclamation marks to inject energy into flat content.
punctuation.fix: Zero exclamations in professional writing; one per 500 words in casual writing.

punctuation.pattern: Rhetorical question immediately followed by the answer
punctuation.tell: AI simulates dialogue with question-answer pairs.
punctuation.fix: Answer directly without the question.

punctuation.pattern: Scare quotes around ordinary words
punctuation.tell: AI adds scare quotes to sound ironic or critical without committing.
punctuation.fix: Drop the quotes; make the judgment in the sentence.

punctuation.pattern: Paragraph content reformatted as bullets
punctuation.tell: AI converts every explanation into a list because lists are lower-risk to generate.
punctuation.fix: Write continuous prose; use lists only for parallel enumerations.

punctuation.pattern: Emoji as list markers or section dividers
punctuation.tell: AI uses emoji bullets to make template content look designed.
punctuation.fix: Real bullets or real sections.

punctuation.pattern: Five or more hashtags at the end of a post
punctuation.tell: AI generates hashtag clouds when asked for social posts.
punctuation.fix: Two or three specific hashtags.

punctuation.pattern: Visible asterisks, underscores, or brackets in chat/email text
punctuation.tell: AI composes in markdown and forgets to render it.
punctuation.fix: Strip markdown markers; use plain text formatting.

punctuation.pattern: Words in ALL CAPS for emphasis instead of sentence-level clarity
punctuation.tell: AI uses caps to simulate shouting-energy.
punctuation.fix: Rewrite the sentence so the emphasis is structural.

punctuation.pattern: Bold applied to whole sentences or phrases repeatedly
punctuation.tell: AI bolds key phrases to create the illusion of structure.
punctuation.fix: Bold at most one phrase per section.

punctuation.pattern: Ordinal numbering where order carries no meaning
punctuation.tell: AI numbers points to look organized even when order is arbitrary.
punctuation.fix: Use bullets for non-sequential items.

punctuation.pattern: Two or more parentheticals per sentence
punctuation.tell: AI stuffs asides into parentheses to keep a single flowing sentence.
punctuation.fix: Split the aside into its own sentence.

punctuation.pattern: Leftover model-output markers: '[1]', '[Source]', 'oaicite', 'turn0search0', 'contentReference'
punctuation.tell: Copy-pasted straight from chat output without cleanup. These strings appear only in LLM citation UIs and rendered chat transcripts; their presence in published text is near-conclusive evidence of unedited model output.
punctuation.fix: Delete the markers and either cite properly or drop the claim.

punctuation.pattern: Unreplaced template slots: '[Your Name]', '[Company]', 'XX%', '[insert statistic]'
punctuation.tell: A draft published before the template was filled. Common when generated content ships straight to a CMS or email tool.
punctuation.fix: Fill every slot, or cut the sentence that needed it.

punctuation.pattern: 'A thread emoji' or '1/', '2/', '3/' on content that is not actually a thread
punctuation.tell: The thread costume: a single post formatted with thread markers for gravity. LinkedIn's slop classifiers key on it.
punctuation.fix: Post a real thread, or delete the markers.

punctuation.pattern: Bold, script, or fullwidth Unicode alphabets across whole lines
punctuation.tell: Unicode bold and script alphabets pasted from special-character tools, mostly in LinkedIn posts. Normal text never uses them; they exist to hijack the feed preview.
punctuation.fix: Use plain text; let the words carry the emphasis.

punctuation.pattern: Curly quotes, non-breaking spaces, or exotic dashes mixed with plain ASCII in the same paragraph
punctuation.tell: Mixed Unicode tells of copy-paste assembly from AI chat interfaces and docs. Clean human drafts are typographically consistent; machine-assembled text is not.
punctuation.fix: Normalize the document to one character set before publishing.

punctuation.pattern: A data table used where one or two sentences would carry the information
punctuation.tell: Formatting substituted for writing, common in AI-generated LinkedIn and blog posts. The table shape signals rigor while holding almost no content.
punctuation.fix: Write the sentence. Keep tables for genuinely tabular data (three or more rows of comparison).
